claims.summary: In a binary Boolean degree-D pseudoideal, fixed A degree<=a,U<=P_K, r fixed inputs degree<=delta>=1 and h>=1 rows, assume a+K+(h+2)delta<=D. For input span B and realized j-row prefix P_j set W_j=image f->(A P_j g_i f) on B^(h-j)U, d_j=dimW_j. Conditional fresh uniform row gives E[d_(j+1)|history]<=d_j/2. If h<=r and coefficient rows are sampled uniformly outside their prior span, the factor is (2^(r-j-1)-1)/(2^(r-j)-1). Thus 2^(-(h-j))d_j is a supermartingale for the first law, and terminal bounds equal existing input-word/independent-row bounds. Subtraction for old-span rows applies to the containing row-kernel intersection, not automatically W_(j+1). Full feature-function saturation has d_j=2^(r-rank C_j)-1, also for the recorded two-layer disjoint-conjunction realization; adaptive selection gives no better universal independent-row factor.
